pages.title: S21 Electrochemical pH sensing
text: **S21 · Chemical observation candidate · Electrochemical measurement**

Electrochemical pH sensing estimates hydrogen-ion activity through an electrode system and a reference potential. The response depends on temperature and on the condition of the sensing and reference interfaces. pH is logarithmic and dimensionless; it is not a direct measure of acid concentration in every sample.
## Signal and useful question

The instrument records an electrical potential, typically in millivolts, and converts it to pH using a qualified calibration. Candidate uses include monitoring a defined liquid research environment or identifying a chemical change that may affect an assay. The measured location must be explicit because a local probe does not describe every region of a plate.
## Interpretation boundary

A pH change can have biological or non-biological causes. Buffer capacity, gas exchange and chemical reactions can alter the relationship between biological activity and the observed value. The system should not label a pH trend as a growth rate or susceptibility result without an independently established model.

This candidate is most suitable for a dedicated research or environmental-monitoring module. Qualification should separate electrode performance from the biological hypothesis. Original voltage, temperature, calibration and derived pH should remain linked so that an investigator can evaluate whether a trend reflects the sample or a changing electrode response.
tables: Appropriate reference buffers, temperature record, response slope and offset.
Reference-junction effects, fouling, ionic composition, temperature, drift and slow equilibration.
Sample contact, cleaning or disposable interfaces, stable reference and electrical isolation.
Reliable local chemical information that matters to the chosen assay or control question.

pages.title: S22 Optical dissolved oxygen sensing
text: **S22 · Chemical and environmental candidate · Optical oxygen measurement**

Optical dissolved-oxygen sensing commonly uses oxygen-dependent quenching of a luminescent indicator. The instrument measures intensity or temporal behaviour and converts it through a calibrated relationship. The sensing element observes its local environment and can respond differently as temperature and the surrounding matrix change.
## Signal and useful question

Outputs may include luminescence phase or lifetime and derived oxygen partial pressure, concentration or percentage saturation. These quantities should not be interchanged without the required conditions and conversion model. Candidate questions include whether a defined research environment remains within its intended oxygen state.
## Link the signal to its location

An oxygen reading near a surface may differ from conditions deeper in a sample. A declining value can reflect transfer limitations as well as consumption. The research model should therefore state the sampled volume or location and distinguish observation from inferred bulk behaviour.

This is a proposed monitoring and research channel. It does not independently establish organism identity or antimicrobial susceptibility. If used in fusion, its time constant and measurement interval should accompany the value so that it is not treated as an instantaneous observation synchronized perfectly with a camera exposure.
tables: Suitable oxygen references, temperature compensation and indicator-response characterization.
Temperature, salinity or matrix effects, indicator ageing, optical background and diffusion lag.
Compatible sensing spot or probe, optical access, sample-contact assessment and local-position records.
A useful local oxygen measurement with an understood response time and maintenance burden.

pages.title: S23 Electrochemical redox potential
text: **S23 · Chemical observation candidate · Redox environment**

Oxidation-reduction potential measures an electrical potential associated with the combined electrochemical environment at a sensing electrode relative to a reference. In complex media, the value can reflect several redox couples and surface processes. It is not generally a selective measurement of one molecule or pathway.
## Signal and useful question

The primary quantity is potential in millivolts, with the reference electrode and temperature identified. A candidate use is monitoring whether a defined research environment changes in a way that merits further investigation or affects assay comparability.
## Avoid mechanistic overreach

Two samples can have similar redox potentials while differing substantially in composition or biological state. Conversely, an electrode-surface change can produce a shift without a meaningful change in the bulk sample. A model should therefore not translate the potential directly into a metabolic identity or a resistance mechanism.

The proposed evaluation should document baseline drift, response time and effects of the permitted medium range. If the channel is used as a quality indicator, define the condition it is intended to detect and the consequence of a missed or false alarm. Its strongest initial role may be contextual monitoring rather than a primary biological inference.
tables: Suitable reference solutions, reference-electrode identity and response stability checks.
Electrode fouling, dissolved gases, medium chemistry, reference drift and slow stabilization.
Contact electrode, cleanable or disposable interface and high-input-impedance measurement circuitry.
Reproducible environmental information with a defensible relationship to the selected research question.

pages.title: S24 Capacitive dielectric sensing
text: **S24 · Physical observation candidate · Dielectric response**

Capacitive dielectric sensing measures how an electric field interacts with the materials between or near electrodes. The response depends on permittivity, geometry, frequency and losses. Water content and container position can strongly influence a biological sample measurement.
## Signal and useful question

Candidate outputs include capacitance in farads at an appropriate scale, conductance and derived dielectric descriptors. Potential uses include detecting presence, monitoring a reproducible physical change or investigating whether a sample’s electrical properties contain useful research information.
## Separate presence from biology

A reliable detector of a plate or liquid level can be useful even if it provides no biological information. That engineering function should be evaluated independently from a proposed growth or composition inference. Counting the same channel as both a presence check and a biological sensor does not create two independent measurements.

This candidate requires a carefully defined operating geometry. Qualification should determine how much signal change is caused by normal placement variation before attributing a similar change to the sample. Where a derived dielectric feature is used in AI, the original measurement settings and quality state should remain available for review and reanalysis.
tables: Reference capacitors or materials, electrode geometry, frequency response and shielding.
Humidity, temperature, vessel wall thickness, position, parasitic capacitance and sample conductivity.
Stable electrodes, guarded circuitry, mechanical repeatability and a clear contact or non-contact interface.
Signal changes that remain interpretable after geometry and environmental effects are controlled.

pages.title: S25 Metal oxide gas sensing
text: **S25 · Chemical observation candidate · Broad gas-response research**

Metal-oxide gas sensors change electrical resistance in response to interactions at a heated sensing surface. Their response can depend on several gases, humidity, temperature, exposure history and the heater programme. A broad gas-response pattern is not a species-specific chemical analysis. Manufacturer documentation supports the underlying gas-sensing capability, not a microbial diagnostic claim. [R17] [R18]
## Signal and useful question

The primary output is resistance or conductance with associated operating conditions. A derived feature may summarize a response over time. The research question is whether controlled headspace observations add reproducible information after medium, cleaning agents and environmental conditions are accounted for.
## Bound the “AI nose” concept

The informal phrase describes pattern analysis of gas responses. It should not imply a measured resistance gene, a unique pathogen identity or a validated AST result. Several sensors exposed to the same uncontrolled headspace can agree for the same wrong reason.

This is a research-only biological inference candidate. A useful development outcome might instead be detection of an instrument contamination event or a changed sampling condition. The intended function should be selected from evidence rather than inferred from the sensor’s ability to produce a complex response curve.
tables: Defined reference exposures, baseline history, environmental compensation and sensor-to-sensor comparison.
Humidity, medium volatiles, carryover, cleaning chemicals, ageing and mixed gas responses.
Controlled sampling path, exposure timing, recovery management and separation from electronics heat.
Transferable information beyond environmental or batch identity, with manageable drift.

pages.title: S26 Photoacoustic gas spectroscopy
text: **S26 · Chemical observation candidate · Photoacoustic gas measurement**

Photoacoustic spectroscopy converts absorbed, modulated optical energy into a pressure-related acoustic signal. With a suitable wavelength and measurement cell, the response can support gas analysis. Selectivity depends on the optical absorption being addressed, the gas mixture and the instrument model.
## Signal and useful question

The primary signal is an acoustic or pressure-related response, converted to a concentration or partial-pressure estimate through calibration. Candidate uses include monitoring a relevant gas in a controlled research environment where the measurement adds more specificity than a broad gas-response sensor.
## Qualify the sampling chain

A precise sensor cannot correct an unrepresentative gas sample. The record should identify where gas was sampled, the flow or diffusion arrangement and the response interval. A delayed signal should not be assigned to the current plate state without a model of that delay.

This modality is a candidate for specialized monitoring or research instruments. Even a well-qualified gas concentration does not identify the biological source of that gas by itself. A biological interpretation requires an appropriate assay and controls that distinguish sample activity from medium, background and instrument contributions.
tables: Reference gas mixtures, optical power, pressure, temperature and acoustic-cell response.
Overlapping absorption, water vapour, background acoustics, leaks and sampling-path memory.
Modulated source, optical cell, acoustic detection, gas routing and environmental correction.
Required gas selectivity and sensitivity with a qualified sampling path.

pages.title: S27 Nondispersive infrared carbon dioxide sensing
text: **S27 · Environmental and research candidate · Infrared gas absorption**

Nondispersive infrared gas sensing measures attenuation in selected infrared bands associated with a target gas, commonly using a reference channel or other compensation. Carbon dioxide monitoring can provide useful environmental context, but the concentration observed depends on sampling location, ventilation and background sources.
## Signal and useful question

The output may be gas concentration in parts per million or volume fraction, with pressure and temperature conditions relevant to the conversion. Candidate questions include whether an instrument environment remains within its declared range and whether a research headspace changes reproducibly.
## Avoid inappropriate baseline correction

Some compensation strategies assume that the sensor periodically sees a known background condition. That assumption may be invalid in a controlled chamber or specialized research setting. The selected device and software configuration should therefore be assessed together.

Carbon dioxide observations may support environmental quality checks or a bounded research model. They do not independently measure viable count or susceptibility. If a biological interpretation is investigated, the model should account for transport, volume, exchange and non-biological sources rather than treating concentration as a direct growth curve.
tables: Suitable gas references, optical baseline, pressure and temperature compensation.
Humidity, optical contamination, leaks, human breath, background drift and automatic baseline assumptions.
Representative gas access, response-time characterization and protection of the optical path.
Stable environmental measurement with a sampling arrangement appropriate to the intended function.

pages.title: S28 Surface acoustic wave mass sensing
text: **S28 · Surface observation candidate · Acoustic-wave research**

Surface acoustic wave devices propagate an acoustic disturbance along a material surface. Changes in the surface environment can alter frequency, phase, velocity or attenuation. A functional coating or sample contact can make the response sensitive to mass loading or material properties, but also introduces additional sources of variation.
## Signal and useful question

Outputs include frequency shift in hertz, phase and attenuation. Candidate research questions concern whether a controlled surface interaction produces a reproducible signal that is useful for the selected assay or environmental measurement.
## Treat selectivity as an assay property

A transducer does not become biologically selective merely because it is highly sensitive. If a surface chemistry is used to create selectivity, that chemistry, its stability and its cross-reactions become part of the assay that must be evaluated.

This is a future research candidate with substantial integration uncertainty. It is not proposed as a direct replacement for whole-plate imaging. The first development task would be to establish a reproducible physical response on controlled reference materials, followed by an assessment of whether the intended biological question can be addressed without confounding the signal with surface or fluid properties.
tables: Frequency and phase reference, temperature response, baseline coating and controlled loading.
Temperature, humidity, viscosity, coating ageing, nonspecific adsorption and mechanical stress.
Specialized transducer, radio-frequency electronics, surface preparation and a qualified sample interface.
A stable response with a defensible separation between intended loading and environmental effects.

pages.title: S29 Quartz crystal microbalance sensing
text: **S29 · Surface observation candidate · Resonant mass and viscoelastic response**

A quartz crystal microbalance detects changes in a resonator’s behaviour when its surface environment changes. Under restricted thin, rigid loading assumptions, frequency shifts can be related to mass per area. In liquids or soft biological layers, viscoelastic and hydrodynamic effects can make a simple mass conversion inappropriate.
## Signal and useful question

The primary outputs are resonant frequency and, where measured, dissipation or related damping quantities. A mass-per-area estimate is derived under an explicit model. Candidate research uses concern controlled surface attachment or material changes rather than weighing an entire culture plate.
## Retain the measured response

The record should preserve frequency and damping data even when the analysis reports an inferred mass. A reviewer should be able to see which model was used and whether the data were consistent with its assumptions. An apparent mass change should not be labelled biomass without an independent basis.

The modality is an exploratory research option. Its qualification should first distinguish surface loading from changes in the surrounding fluid. Clinical susceptibility or organism identification would require a separate assay and validation programme, and neither follows from the resonator’s nominal mass sensitivity alone.
tables: Frequency reference, clean-surface baseline, temperature stability and suitable loading models.
Liquid viscosity, density, soft-film behaviour, nonspecific adsorption and surface history.
Resonator interface, stable fluid or contact conditions, surface management and specialized electronics.
A reproducible response whose model assumptions remain credible in the selected sample format.

pages.title: S30 Acoustic resonance and attenuation
text: **S30 · Physical observation candidate · Acoustic material response**

Acoustic resonance and attenuation measurements examine how sound propagates through or interacts with a material system. The observed response depends on geometry, density, compressibility, viscosity and interfaces. In a plate or fluid assembly, vessel properties can contribute strongly to the signal.
## Signal and useful question

Candidate outputs include resonant frequency in hertz, sound velocity in metres per second, attenuation and dimensionless quality factor. Potential research questions include whether a reproducible physical change can be detected and separated from the mechanical properties of the holder and vessel.
## Establish a useful baseline first

An assembly may have many resonances unrelated to the sample. Development should characterize the empty holder and permitted vessels before interpreting changes in a biological context. The analysis should retain the excitation and detection conditions so that a spectral shift can be investigated later.

This is a future research candidate, with no AMReye.AI assay evidence established here. It may prove more useful for checking fill state, mechanical coupling or instrument integrity than for biological inference. Selection should follow the demonstrated function rather than the general sensitivity of acoustic methods.
tables: Known mechanical or fluid references, geometry, coupling and frequency response.
Temperature, bubbles, contact pressure, vessel variation, mounting and background vibration.
Transducers, coupling arrangement, excitation control and stable mechanical interfaces.
A signal linked to the intended physical change with acceptable sensitivity to placement.
